title: Header Search
description:
The header's fold-out search — live's `#masthead #searchform`, which is already a disclosure: the `.search-field` sits at `width: 20px; opacity: 0` behind a 20px magnifier and unrolls on a `0.4s ease-in-out` transition. Measured on live 2026-08-20. Replaces the `.sd-header__search` class the treatment used to be configured by, so it is now chosen from the block's Styles panel like every other style in this theme.

## No JavaScript, and none needed

On WordPress 7.0 `core/search` is expandable natively whenever `buttonPosition` is `button-only`: wp-includes/blocks/search.php enqueues the Interactivity view module, binds `aria-expanded` and `aria-label` on the button, and toggles `wp-block-search__searchfield-hidden` **on the form** via `data-wp-class`. Escape and focus-out close it. The disclosure, its ARIA and its keyboard behaviour are all core's; the theme only draws it. (`isSearchFieldHidden` is a pre-Interactivity leftover, no longer in core's block.json — don't set it.)

## What is here, and what is in CSS

Here: the trigger's design. `core/search` runs its button through `wp_theme_get_element_class_name('button')`, so it is a real `.wp-element-button` and would otherwise inherit theme.json's brand-500 ground, padding and radius and render as a large orange tile. Structured `elements.button` rather than a `css` field so the editor renders it and so the field's `:hover` strip doesn't apply.

The fold-out mechanism — the panel's geometry and its open/closed states, the icon sizing, the reduced-motion opt-out — is in assets/styles/core-search.css, scoped to `.is-style-header-search`. It is long, stateful, and one part of it (`@media`) cannot compile in a `css` field at all. A `css` field big enough to hold all of it is a JSON string nobody can read or diff, which is how this drifted the first time.

Border is deliberately **not** a structured property on the panel either: `core/search`'s `selectors.border` covers `.wp-block-search__button-only .wp-block-search__input` *and* `… .wp-block-search__button`, so a structured border would draw a box around the bare magnifier as well as the panel.

## css field limits, measured on WP 7.0, 2026-08-21

For whoever adds to this later. Survives: `&`, `&.class`, `&:not(.class)`, `& .a`, `& .a .b`, commas inside declaration values (`min()`, `cubic-bezier()`, multi-part `transition`), and structured `elements.button` with `:hover`/`:focus`. Does **not** survive: `@media` — it compiles to a dead `:root :where(.is-style-header-search--N@media (max-width: 960px)){}` plus the inner rule emitted unconditionally at every width, which is silently wrong rather than silently absent. The theme's skill reference claimed `@media` survives; it does not, and the reference has been corrected.

## Below 781px the panel is in flow

The out-of-flow panel sized itself as `min(600px, 100vw - spacing-80)`, which is a guess at the room to the *left of the icon* written as a fraction of the whole viewport — and the icon is not at the viewport's edge. Measured on local 2026-08-28, the open panel's left edge sat at **-61px** at 390px and -59px at 600px; nothing scrolled, so the overhang was simply cut off. Below core's 781px column-stacking breakpoint the form now grows across the row and the panel returns to normal flow inside it, so it stops at the root gutter by construction rather than by arithmetic. One style, not two — the treatment, its ARIA and its tokens are unchanged. The mechanism is in assets/styles/core-search.css with the reasoning; `@media` still cannot compile here.
